title: Memo: How reliable is the classification pipeline at scale?

yaml.title: Memo: How reliable is the classification pipeline at scale?
yaml.subtitle: Research memorandum — failure-pipeline simulation
author: Jack J. Burleson
Grant Mooslin

markdown.markdown:
**Research question:** What fraction of rows fail to produce a usable prediction, and does the retry/fallback pipeline keep the failure rate tolerable when extrapolated to 800 / 25,000 / 320,000 images?

**Formal write-up:** [`montecarlo/failure-pipeline.qmd`](../montecarlo/failure-pipeline.html) · [`reports/monte_carlo/failure_pipeline.md`](https://github.com/Exios66/AMFAM_capstone/blob/main/reports/monte_carlo/failure_pipeline.md)

---


**With fallback enabled, the pipeline failure rate is ~0.11% — a 24× reduction over the observed 2.72% single-pass rate.** The fitted model: *P*(first success) = 0.946, provider transient/quota 429 failures ≈ 0, `max_tries` = 3, two API keys, fallback on.

| Scale | Expected failures | 95% *CI* | *P*(>1%) | *P*(>5%) |
|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| 800 | 1 | 0–3 | 0.000 | 0.000 |
| 25,000 | 28 | 19–39 | 0.000 | 0.000 |
| 320,000 | 364 | 328–402 | 0.000 | 0.000 |

The dominant failure driver is the **first-attempt success rate** (94.6%), not retry count. Sensitivity sweep:

| max_tries | fallback | failure rate | attempts/row |
|---:|---|---:|---:|
| 1 | off | 2.940% | 1.03 |
| 1 | **on** | **0.114%** | 1.06 |
| 3 | on | 0.114% | 1.06 |
| 5 | on | 0.114% | 1.06 |

::: {.callout-important title="Fallback is the Key"}
Adding a fallback key reduces failure ~**24×**; raising `max_tries` beyond 3 adds nothing because the residual failures are persistent (content-filter / token-cap), not transient.
:::

**Conclusion.** The pipeline is **production-safe for failures**: even at 320K images, expected failures ≈ 364 with *P*(>5%) ≈ 0. Per-row failure rows are handled as explicit misses (the `failure` Braintrust scorer), so they do not silently contaminate accuracy.

::: {.memo-sources}
*Sources:* `reports/monte_carlo/failure_pipeline.md` · `src/evaluation.py` (ManifestStore resume) · [github.com/Exios66/AMFAM_capstone](https://github.com/Exios66/AMFAM_capstone)
:::

---

## What questions or uncertainties remain?

The model is fitted on `qwen3.7-flash`-specific failure data; other providers (gemini, kimi) have different transient/429 profiles and were not fitted. The 94.6% first-success rate will drift with provider status and prompt length (longer v11.8+ prompts push token caps). The residual failures are persistent, so no retry policy eliminates them — only a fundamentally different fallback (e.g., a cheaper non-reasoning model) would.

## What other levers may also improve accuracy?

Failure rows are separate from accuracy misses; the accuracy levers are covered in the [hardest-classes](hardest-classes.qmd), [ensemble](ensemble-voting.qmd), and [confidence-routing](confidence-routing.qmd) memos.
